summary: P. De Lacy Johnstone (1848–1927) was an Indology scholar. He studied at the University of Edinburgh and the University of Oxford, earning his B.A. and M.A. from Balliol College, Oxford (1868–1876), and serving as a Boden Sanskrit Scholar (~1867–1871).
P. H. Joshi is an Indologist who served as a Research Officer at the Oriental Institute, Vadodara (attested 1976–1988), where a post is also attested in 2002.

P. K. Mukhopadhyay is a scholar of philosophy and Indology. He served as a Professor of Philosophy at Jadavpur University and was a National Fellow at the Indian Council of Philosophical Research (attested 2009).

P. N. Pattabhirama Sastri (1908–1992) was a scholar in Indology and philosophy who studied under A. Chinnaswami Sastri and taught Elliot M. Stern. He held posts at Banaras Hindu University (attested 1941) and the University of Calcutta (attested 1963).

Pramod P. Joglekar is an archaeologist and Indologist. He served on the Regulating Council and as Editor at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (2020–2025) and is attested as Professor of Bioarchaeology at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (2026).

P. P. Subrahmanya Sastri, an Indologist, studied at the University of Madras (M.A.) and Oxford (B.A.). He was Head of Sanskrit at Presidency University, Professor at Presidency College, Chennai (attested 1937–1944), and Curator at the Government Oriental Manuscripts Library (attested 1937).
P. Perumal, who works in Indology and history/archaeology, earned an M.L.I.Sc from Madurai Kamaraj University in 1985. He held a post as a part-time Conservator at Saraswathi Mahal Library in 1980.
P. Pratap Kumar (b. 1952) is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. In 2010, he was attested as a Professor at the University of KwaZulu-Natal and as a Visiting Professor at Colorado College.
P. S. Chandrasekharan is an Indology scholar who was attested in 2026 as a Ph.D. scholar at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute under the doctoral supervision of V. Yamuna Devi.

P. S. Subrahmanya Sastri (1890–1978) studied at Bishop Heber College, IASE Saidapet, and the University of Madras (Ph.D.). He headed Sanskrit at Bishop Heber and Annamalai University, served at Rajah's College and University of Madras, and taught Thomas Burrow.
P. Swaminathan is an Indologist who completed an M.Litt. at the University of Madras in 1956 under V. Raghavan. He was attested as a Lecturer in Sanskrit at National Sanskrit University in 1965.
P. T. Narasimhachar (1905–1998) worked in Indology and other fields. He studied at Maharaja's College, Mysore (~1923–1927), where he was taught by Mysore Hiriyanna.
P. V. Ramanujaswami was an Indology scholar who served as Director and अध्यक्षः at the Sri Venkateswara Oriental Research Institute, with posts attested in 1944 and 1954.

Padma Subrahmanyam (b. 1943) is a scholar in Indology and history/archaeology. She studied at Ethiraj College for Women, Stella Maris College, and Annamalai University (~1974–1979) under research supervisor T. N. Ramachandran.

Padmanabh S. Jaini (1923–2021) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under John Brough. He served as Professor and Professor Emeritus at the University of California, Berkeley, and taught numerous prominent scholars.
Pagorn Singsuriya is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Chulalongkorn University and held a post in the Humanities at Mahidol University (attested 2021).

Palden Gyal works in Tibetology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He earned degrees from Duke (B.A.), Harvard (M.A.), and Columbia (Ph.D.), where he was attested in 2026 as a Postdoctoral Fellow at the Heyman Center for the Humanities.

Pallabi Bagchi works in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She earned a B.A. from Jadavpur University and a Ph.D. from Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda, where she served as a teaching assistant from 2022 to 2025.
Palmer Boyd (1840–1875) was an Indologist who studied at Trinity College (B.A. 1867–1871) under Edward Byles Cowell. He later held a post at Trinity College, Cambridge.

Palmira Brummett (b. 1950) studied at the University of Chicago and the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign. She was a professor at the University of Tennessee, Knoxville (~1989–2011) and a visiting professor at Brown University (2011–2016).
